articles.title: A Florida daughter lost control of her late mother's estate and three family trusts after representing them in court without a lawyer; a November 12 appeals court upheld all four removals despite her objections
articles.summary: Managing a deceased parent's estate and family trusts can involve complex legal responsibilities, particularly when disagreements arise among
articles.body: Managing a deceased parent's estate and family trusts can involve complex legal responsibilities, particularly when disagreements arise among beneficiaries. A Florida daughter who continued representing her late mother's estate and three family trusts in court without a lawyer has now lost all four positions after an appeals court upheld her removal, finding that her actions violated established legal requirements.In a November 12, 2026, decision, the Florida Third District Court of Appeal affirmed four removal orders against Kerrin Friedman. The rulings removed her as personal representative of her mother Bonny L Wax's estate and as trustee of three family trusts. In Kerrin Friedman v. In Re: Estate of Bonny L Wax, available on Justia, the appeals court rejected her arguments that the probate court lacked authority to remove her and had denied her due process.Daughter continued representing estate without a lawyerThe dispute involved four separate probate and trust proceedings in Miami-Dade County. Friedman was appointed personal representative of her late mother's estate and also served as trustee of three trusts connected to her siblings: the Bobbi Ring Trust, the Adam Wax Trust and the Credit Shelter Trust. However, her decision to represent these legal entities herself became a central issue in the proceedings.On April 17, 2025, the probate court ordered Friedman to obtain a lawyer within 30 days to represent her in the estate case. The requirement followed Florida Probate Rule 5.030(a), which generally requires a personal representative to be represented by a Florida attorney unless that person is the estate's sole interested person. Instead of complying, Friedman continued representing herself in the estate proceedings. She also appeared without a lawyer in the appeals court and federal court.Court barred her from representing family trustsThe legal restrictions extended to her role as trustee. On July 3, 2025, the probate court issued an order in the Adam Wax Trust case prohibiting Friedman from representing the trust herself. Under Florida law, a trustee who is not a licensed attorney cannot represent a trust's interests in litigation because doing so constitutes the unauthorised practice of law.Despite the order, Friedman continued filing documents on behalf of the Adam Wax Trust without legal representation. She also began representing herself as trustee in the subsequently filed Bobbi Ring Trust and Credit Shelter Trust proceedings. Meanwhile, the other parties involved in the trust cases sought her removal, raising several allegations of misconduct in their motions.Probate court ordered removal from all four positionsAt a September 16, 2025, hearing, the probate court announced that it would remove Friedman as personal representative of her mother's estate and as trustee of all three family trusts. The court cited her continued unauthorised self-representation, among other grounds. It subsequently entered formal removal orders in all four proceedings.Friedman challenged the decisions, arguing that the probate court lacked statutory authority to remove her from the positions. She also claimed that the September hearing violated her right to due process.Appeals court rejects daughter's objectionsThe Florida Third District Court of Appeal rejected both arguments. On the due-process issue, the judges noted that Friedman had received notice of the September 16 hearing and had an opportunity to present her position. The court therefore found no basis to conclude that she had been denied a fair opportunity to be heard. The appeals court also explained that Florida law expressly authorises probate courts to remove personal representatives in certain circumstances.Under Florida Probate Rule 5.440(a), a probate court may remove a personal representative on its own initiative. Section 733.504(3) of the Florida Statutes also permits removal when a personal representative violates a court order. The judges found that Friedman had violated the April 17 order requiring her to retain legal counsel.Regarding the three trusts, the court relied on Section 736.0706 of the Florida Statutes, which allows a court to remove a trustee under specified circumstances, including when the trustee has committed a serious breach of trust or other grounds justify removal. The judges explained that a non-lawyer trustee cannot represent a trust in litigation. Friedman's continued attempts to do so, despite the court's July 3 order, provided sufficient grounds for her removal.All four removal orders upheldThe appeals court clarified that it did not need to decide whether the separate allegations of misconduct raised against Friedman were justified. Her unauthorised self-representation alone provided sufficient grounds for the probate court's decisions. It ultimately affirmed all four removal orders, leaving Friedman without control over her mother's estate or the three family trusts.The November 12 ruling addresses her authority to serve in these legal roles and does not determine the merits of the separate misconduct allegations raised by the other parties. The opinion is not final until any timely motion for rehearing has been resolved.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Estonia opens the Baltics’ largest heat storage tower in Tallinn, a 42-metre structure holding 20,000 cubic metres of hot water and storing 1,100 megawatt-hours of heat
articles.summary: Estonian energy company Utilitas opened the largest thermal storage facility in the Baltic states in February 2026, a 42-metre tower at the Väo energy
articles.body: Estonian energy company Utilitas opened the largest thermal storage facility in the Baltic states in February 2026, a 42-metre tower at the Väo energy complex in Tallinn that stores 1,100 megawatt-hours of heat as hot water for the city’s district heating network. The company announced the opening on 6 February. It is the first large-scale heat accumulator in the Estonian capital, and the Swedish company Granitor Rodoverken, now part of the industrial services provider Bilfinger, built it for 8 million euros. Its construction was co-financed with 675,000 euros from the European Union’s NextGenerationEU recovery instrument through Estonia’s Environmental Investment Centre.Inside the Väo heat storage tower: 20,000 cubic metres of water, nearly eight Olympic poolsAccording to Utilitas, the tower is 26 metres in diameter and holds 20,000 cubic metres of water, which the company says matches the volume of nearly eight full-size Olympic swimming pools. It lists the facility’s power capacity at 80 megawatts. The tower is designed to smooth out the day’s heat production, storing heat when it is not needed and releasing it when consumption is high.Priit Koit, chief executive of the Utilitas Group, said at the opening that “storage plays a very important role” in an energy industry where flexibility and efficiency are increasingly important. He said it helps the system respond to changing consumption, raises production efficiency and strengthens security of supply, and that it is needed in both electricity and heat networks. At the Väo complex, green energy is produced by two high-efficiency combined heat and power plants and two solar parks.Tallinn’s mayor said the storage tower makes district heating more reliable for residentsPeeter Raudsepp, Mayor of Tallinn, said at the opening that being able to store heat and use it when consumption is high strengthens the reliability of the district heating network. He said a more flexible and stable network is in the interest of every resident. He argued that investments should continue, because this one served consumers and security of supply while also being economically sensible.The company said in February that storage helps reduce fossil fuel use, which in turn supports stable prices. It said it had also completed a thermal storage facility in the city of Jõgeva earlier in 2026 and planned to build two more in Tallinn during the year, at the Mustamäe combined heat and power plant and the Paljassaare heat pump plant.In a later update on its first-quarter results, the company said further thermal storage units, along with the Paljassaare heat pump plant and new electric boilers, are still under construction.You use AI every day. articles.title: Hospital charity executive accused of approving $3.6 million in fake invoices and pocketing $1 million in kickbacks; alleged purchases included Louis Vuitton bags and a rose-gold golf cart
articles.summary: Financial misconduct allegations involving a hospital charity have drawn attention to how money intended for healthcare fundraising can be diverted
articles.body: Financial misconduct allegations involving a hospital charity have drawn attention to how money intended for healthcare fundraising can be diverted through seemingly routine business payments. In Miami, federal prosecutors have accused a former senior executive of Jackson Health Foundation of approving millions of dollars in invoices for goods and services that were never supplied. The alleged scheme involved a Georgia-based audiovisual company, a merchandise supplier and payments that investigators say benefited the executive personally. As reported by The Department of Justice, among the purchases described in the indictment were luxury items from Louis Vuitton and Gucci, Apple products and a rose-gold golf cart delivered to her home in Florida.Former hospital charity COO accused of taking more than $1 million in kickbacksCharmaine Gatlin, 52, who served as chief operating officer of Jackson Health Foundation between 2014 and 2024, was charged in a federal indictment unsealed on 21 May 2025. Prosecutors allege that she used her position to arrange payments through false invoices and received more than $1 million in kickbacks from a business vendor.The foundation is the fundraising organisation associated with Jackson Health System, a nonprofit hospital network serving Miami-Dade County in Florida. Its work involves collecting philanthropic contributions to support the healthcare system, which also receives funding through sales taxes, federal programmes and other sources.Gatlin held a senior operational position and earned an annual base salary ranging from $185,000 to $290,000, according to the indictment. She had also signed a conflict-of-interest declaration stating that she would not make decisions that could provide her with personal financial benefits.How false invoices allegedly generated $1 million in kickbacksThe indictment describes at least $3.6 million in invoices submitted to Jackson Health Foundation for goods and services that prosecutors say were either never delivered, supplied to Gatlin or her relatives, or directed to an Atlanta-based civic organisation rather than the foundation or hospital system.One of the largest alleged arrangements involved a Georgia-based audiovisual company. According to prosecutors, Gatlin approved approximately $2 million in invoices for work that was not actually carried out for the foundation.The vendor allegedly returned around $1 million to Gatlin through kickback payments. Some of this money was reportedly used to settle her personal credit card bill, turning payments recorded as organisational expenses into funds that benefited her privately.Prosecutors also allege that Gatlin communicated with the audiovisual supplier by email and provided guidance on how to prepare invoices that falsely represented the services being purchased.Louis Vuitton, Gucci and Apple purchases included in the allegationsA separate part of the indictment concerns a merchandise supplier that allegedly purchased expensive personal items at Gatlin's request. Rather than paying for the gifts herself, prosecutors say she arranged for the vendor to acquire the products and submitted false invoices to the foundation to cover their costs.The items included designer goods from Louis Vuitton and Gucci, along with Apple products. The alleged arrangement meant that purchases intended for Gatlin personally were presented through payments made by the nonprofit organisation.The indictment also identifies a rose-gold-coloured golf cart as one of the purchases allegedly covered through this process. According to prosecutors, Gatlin arranged for a false invoice to be submitted for the vehicle, which was delivered to her home in Weston, Florida, in September 2023, as reported by The Department of Justice.$3.6 million in allegedly false invoices over several yearsThe alleged transactions were not limited to one supplier or a single payment. Prosecutors say the invoices submitted during Gatlin's tenure covered at least $3.6 million in goods and services, with several different outcomes for the money.Some payments allegedly funded kickbacks, while others covered products or services that never reached Jackson Health Foundation or its associated hospital system. In other instances, the benefits were directed towards Gatlin's relatives or the Atlanta-based civic organisation identified in the indictment.Federal indictment carries potential prison sentencesGatlin faces 32 federal charges: one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud, 26 counts of wire fraud and five counts of money laundering.The potential penalties are substantial. Each conspiracy and substantive wire fraud count carries a maximum sentence of 20 years in federal prison, while each money laundering count carries a maximum of 10 years. These are statutory maximum penalties, not an indication of the sentence she would receive if convicted.The investigation was conducted by the FBI's Miami office, with assistance from the Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office. US Attorney Hayden P. O'Byrne and acting FBI Miami Special Agent in Charge Brett Skiles announced the charges. Assistant US Attorney Elizabeth Young is handling the prosecution, while Assistant US Attorney G. Raemy Charest-Turken is responsible for asset forfeiture matters.The case was announced by the US Attorney's Office for the Southern District of Florida on 21 May 2025. Gatlin is presumed innocent unless prosecutors establish her guilt in court. An indictment represents formal criminal allegations, not a finding of guilt.You use AI every day. articles.title: Russell Brand: Alleged rape victim wants age of consent law changed
articles.summary: Mia Latter, who says she was 16 when she met the convicted rapist, wants a staggered age of consent.
articles.body:
Warning - this story contains graphic content

A woman who has alleged that she was raped by Russell Brand when she was 16 has waived her right to anonymity and is campaigning for a staggered age of consent in an interview with the Sunday Times.

Mia Latter was one of six women who made allegations against Brand in 2023 as part of a Times, Sunday Times and Channel 4's Dispatches investigation. She was known under the pseudonym 'Alice'. Brand denied the allegations at the time.

None of the women in the 2023 media investigation were complainants in Brand's recent criminal trial.

On Monday the entertainer was sentenced to 10 and a half years for one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. He was acquitted of two counts of rape and one allegation of attempted indecent assault.

The Sunday Times reported that Latter had initially described the allegation about Brand to them as a sexual assault and that is how they reported it in their 2023 investigation.

Latter, 37, "now calls this allegation rape", the paper said.

Latter said she was 16 when she met Brand, who was 30 at the time, when she was on her way home from a shopping trip. She said Brand was working at MTV.

She told the paper: "I think people were so struck by my story because of the age difference and the clear imbalance [in power],"

She said Brand told her to keep their relationship secret from her school friends and claimed that he referred to her as "the child" in front of his entourage.

It was towards the end of their relationship that Latter was allegedly orally raped by Brand, according to the Sunday Times.

Latter said that she was now campaigning for the introduction of a "staggered" age of consent that would prohibit relationships between 16- and 17-year-olds and adults.

"I don't want to criminalise teenagers having sex with each other," she told the paper. "If you're between the ages of 16 and 18, it seems reasonable that you can have relationships with each other, and [teenagers] are always going to. But … if you're in your thirties, forties and fifties and you're trying to have a relationship with someone under the age of 18, it [should be] a criminal offence."

She also told the paper that she would not continue with the criminal process so she could focus on her campaign.

In her interview with the Sunday Times she said that the CPS decided not to include her as part of Brand's criminal trial but the police wanted her to be part of a "subsequent trial".

A Met Police spokesperson said: "Officers launched an investigation in January 2026 after receiving an allegation of rape.

"Detectives sought advice from the Crown Prosecution Service to determine how best to proceed, and officers were advised that further information was needed before a charging decision could be made.

"This investigation remains ongoing. We understand the delay has been distressing for this victim-survivor. However, our focus has been on putting forward the best possible evidence."

A spokesperson for the Crown Prosecution Service said it would "continue to work closely with investigators to provide advice and make sure cases progress as quickly as possible".

articles.title: Pak sending 'experienced' minister for Delhi event
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Pakistan announced on Saturday that it will participate in the inaugural Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue,
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Pakistan announced on Saturday that it will participate in the inaugural Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue, scheduled to be held in New Delhi from November 20 to 22. Prime Minister Narendra Modi had proposed the dialogue at the SCO summit in Tianjin in 2025.The last visit by a Pakistani minister to India was in May 2023, when then Foreign Minister Bilawal Bhutto Zardari travelled to Goa to attend a meeting of SCO foreign ministers. This will also be the first ministerial visit between the two countries since the Pahalgam terror attack last year.Pakistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said that Musadik Masood Malik, Federal Minister for Climate Change and Environmental Coordination, will lead the country’s delegation to the dialogue.India had invited culture minister Aurangzeb Khichi for the event. Musadik Masood Malik, federal minister for climate change and environmental coordination, will lead the team. He however, is considered a more experienced minister in the Pakistan govt. "The event will bring together representatives from SCO member states to exchange views on issues related to civilisational dialogue and cultural understanding," said Pakistan in its announcement, adding that Islamabad remains committed to promoting dialogue among civilisations and fostering people-to-people ties within the SCO framework in a spirit of mutual respect.After Bilawal's visit in 2023, external affairs minister S Jaishankar had visited Pakistan the next year, again for a meeting of SCO foreign ministers. On both occasions, there was no bilateral meeting between the ministers.Even in the absence of any substantive bilateral engagement for over a decade, both countries have continued to interact within the Eurasian bloc which they both joined as full members in 2017.Pakistan currently holds the SCO presidency and will host the heads of state summit next year. articles.title: Meet the hooded pitohui, the world's poisonous bird whose feathers and skin carry a powerful toxin whose touch can leave humans numb; where to spot it
articles.summary: Deep inside the tropical rainforests of New Guinea lives a bird that looks almost too beautiful to be deadly!
articles.body: Deep inside the tropical rainforests of New Guinea lives a bird that looks almost too beautiful to be deadly! She is bright, she has an orange-chestnut body and a gorgeous glossy black head and wings are so beautiful. Meet hooded pitohui (Pitohui dichrous) which is reportedly the only bird on Earth with a toxic death touch! Yes, you read that right. The bird’s feathers and skin carry a powerful neurotoxin belonging to the same chemical family found in some of the world's most poisonous frogs.Imagine just touching this bird and feeling a burning sensation and numbness which can soon turn fatal.Meet hooded pitohuiAlso known as the world's poisonous bird, the hooded pitohui became a scientific sensation when researchers discovered that it carried toxins in its feathers and skin which can cause death. However, it is not technically the only poisonous bird on Earth.Other New Guinea species, including the variable pitohui and the blue-capped ifrita. This bird too has similar toxins. As per a 1992 study published in the journal Science by ornithologist John P. Dumbacher and his colleagues, three species of pitohui contained homobatrachotoxin, a powerful chemical previously associated with poison-dart frogs.Why is the hooded pitohui considered poisonousThere is a group of chemicals called batrachotoxins which are potent steroidal alkaloid neurotoxins that interfere with voltage-gated sodium channels in nerve and muscle cells.The consequences can be severe. Depending on the exposure and dose, these toxins can cause tingling, burning sensations, numbness, muscular problems and potentially life-threatening effects.The 1992 research found that toxin concentrations were highest in the hooded pitohui's skin and feathers. This explains why the bird's touch has attracted so much attention.During the original research, scientists experienced burning, sneezing and numbness after handling specimens. The effects were particularly noticeable when they came into contact with their mouths and nasal tissues.The expression 'death touch' is sensationalThere is no established evidence that simply touching a hooded pitohui kills a person. The documented human reactions include irritation, burning and numbness, while the toxins themselves are capable of causing severe toxicity at sufficient doses.Where to spot hooded pitohuiThe hooded pitohui is native to the island of New Guinea, which is shared by Indonesia and Papua New Guinea.Its habitat includes tropical rainforests, hill forests and lower montane forests. It can be found at different forest levels, from the understorey to the canopy, where it searches for food.For birdwatchers hoping to spot one, Papua New Guinea is an important destination. The bird has been recorded in places such as Varirata National Park, near Port Moresby, and in forested regions of Morobe Province.The hooded pitohui is approximately 22–23 cm long. Its striking appearance makes identification relatively easy: it has a black head, throat, upper breast, wings and tail, contrasting with rich orange-chestnut plumage across its back and lower body.How does the bird acquire its poison?One of the most fascinating aspects of the hooded pitohui is that it does not appear to manufacture its poison independently.Scientists believe it obtains the toxins through its diet. Research has linked the presence of batrachotoxins in these birds to their consumption of small beetles belonging to the genus Choresine.These beetles contain compounds that the birds can accumulate in their bodies. The toxins are subsequently found in their skin and feathers, making contact potentially unpleasant for predators and other animals.Other poisonous birds in the worldBesides the hooded pitohui, there is the blue-capped ifrita. It is a small bird found in the mountainous forests of New Guinea. Researchers discovered batrachotoxins in its skin and feathers in a study published in PNAS in 2000.For humans, the lesson is straightforward: the hooded pitohui may look like an ordinary forest songbird, but it is certainly not one to handle casually.You use AI every day. articles.title: Tanker ‘lost control’ and hit cruise ship in New Orleans, spurring massive evacuation, officials say
articles.summary: Emergency responders rushed to the New Orleans waterfront after a tanker “lost control” and hit a river cruise boat, causing a mass evacuation of over 130 pe...
articles.body:
Passengers of a river cruise boat in New Orleans had to be pulled from the Mississippi river on Friday after a tanker collided with the paddlewheeler as it sat in dock, causing it to capsize.

Those aboard desperately gripped the railings of the American Heritage as it started taking on water and tipping over, sparking a major emergency response.

In what Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry hailed as a "miracle on the Mississippi," all 197 passengers made it to safety.

"There had to be some kind of divine, godly intervention for this outcome," Mayor Helena Moreno said Saturday.

Hours after the collision, the Port of New Orleans sued to ensure the seizure of the tanker, Atlantic Asphalt, which the lawsuit said is owned and managed by a Liberia-based shipping company.

The lawsuit, which also named Thome Ship Management in Singapore, said the tanker caused more than $1 million in damage to a New Orleans terminal.

The docked riverboat was struck "as a result of the negligence, gross negligence, fault or carelessness" of the tanker, Nave Shipping and Thome, according to the suit. CNN has reached out to Thome for comment and is attempting to contact the tanker's owner.

Moreno said 32 people were taken to hospitals with noncritical injuries, while others were treated at the scene for "bumps and bruises." On Saturday, city officials said eight remained in hospitals – two in serious condition, the others stable.

The Atlantic Asphalt appeared to have "lost control," according to US Coast Guard Captain Melanie Burnham, who added that the "exact reason why" it may have lost steering capabilities remained unknown.

"I do not have any indication that this is terrorism-related," Burnham added.

Investigators are on scene collecting evidence and plan to begin interviewing crew members in the coming days, National Transportation Safety Board officials said in a Saturday afternoon news briefing.

In dramatic video from the scene, a distinct metallic screech can be heard as the vessels collide. At least a dozen people wearing life vests can later be seen being pulled from the water, while other passengers clamber over the railings of the boat, lying on its side in the Mississippi.

About 80 people were evacuated from the boat before it capsized, said New Orleans Harbor Police Chief Melanie Montroll.

Numerous vessels immediately rushed to the scene to rescue passengers from the river.

"It was all hands on deck," the mayor said. "First responders, other boats and vessels that were in proximity all raced to do what they could to help," Moreno told reporters.

Joe Knab, a passenger visiting New Orleans from Wichita, told CNN affiliate WDSU the hulking tanker was blasting its horn as it floated toward the riverboat. Moments later, he was in the water without a life jacket, clutching a pillow to stay afloat and a woman holding onto his feet.

"It was a little scary there at the time when I think I was drowning because I kept bobbing underneath," he said, adding he was in the water for 15 to 20 minutes.

Knab wore a T-shirt from a Hilton hotel where passengers stayed Friday night. His other shirts and belongings were "at the bottom of the river," he said.

"My phone still works. That's amazing. I got my wallet," he said. His roommate on the boat, however, lost everything.

Truck driver Blas Armas, who recorded on his phone as panicked passengers tried to swim from the stricken boat, said many elderly people in the river screamed, "Help, help."

"The most terrifying thing was an old lady (who had) only her head out of the water," Armas told CNN late Friday. "She was wearing a vest, but it wasn't around her neck," he said, adding that she was trying to swim with one hand as she clung to what looked like a piece of floating furniture. The woman was eventually pulled to safety.

He also recalled seeing an elderly man bleeding from his forehead. "People were scared," he said.

Brian Clesi, captain of the New Orleans riverboat Creole Queen, was on his way to work Friday when he received a phone call: A ship had lost steering about a quarter mile away. Clesi and Ellis "Jimmy" Kimball later launched the riverboat's bow-mounted rescue boat and made their way to the crash site, where rescuers were already plucking people from the river.

Clesi, 53, told CNN he and his partner pulled nine people out of the water and took them to other vessels for triage or to first responders on the riverbank. They brought one man with head trauma to a fireboat.

"About three people we responded to, including one harbor police officer, were wearing life jackets. But the rest that we pulled out were not. So, it was imperative to get them to safety as soon as possible," Clesi said.

"I'm just glad we were there to get them out," he said. "The ones that didn't have a life jacket on were holding on for dear life."

Many of the people in the water were elderly and appeared to be in shock, Clesi said.

"We train for this. We do man overboard drills, rescue drills, fire drills," Clesi said. "Everybody in this harbor works together as a team. If somebody is in need, everybody's coming. So, it wasn't just us. We played a very small part in the grand scheme of things."

Moreno, the mayor, said passengers began disembarking after the cruise ship was first hit, but it then began to sink and eventually "toppled over and flipped."

New Orleans firefighters immediately responded to the collision and used ladders over the dock to try to rescue people, Moreno said. Other ships on the Mississippi River also responded to help get people out of the water, she added.

American Cruise Lines, the owner of the riverboat American Heritage, confirmed its boat was involved in the incident and said it worked with local authorities to evacuate everyone from the vessel.

Thome, the ship management company responsible for implementing the International Safety Management code on the boat, said in a statement that the Atlantic Asphalt tanker was built in 2017 and registered in the Marshall Islands.

"We deeply regret the impact of this incident and extend our sincere concern and heartfelt sympathies to those injured. Our thoughts remain with the passengers of the AMERICAN HERITAGE following their harrowing experience as we work diligently to assess and investigate the incident," the company said, adding that it was "fully complying with the local authorities."

The American Heritage was built in 2015 and has capacity for 150 guests, according to the operator . The cruise line, which offers river cruises across the US, hosts several cruises that port in New Orleans.

The person driving the tanker was a river pilot, said Burnham, the Coast Guard captain.

Some passengers abandoned personal items on the sinking ship, Moreno said, and are now staying at local hotels. The city is working with partners, including the American Red Cross, to ensure all passengers have access to accommodation, transportation and necessary prescription medications.

Two harbor police officers that had been hospitalized were released Friday evening, the Port of New Orleans said in an update.

Landry, the governor, praised all of the agencies involved, saying their constant partnership prepared them for this type of situation.

"It is a literal miracle on the Mississippi," he said. "When you think about the population that was on that cruise ship, and the ability for us to get them off, get them out of the water."

"The Mississippi River is not some quiet pond, right? I mean, there were challenges out there," he added.

President Donald Trump, who offered the state support, also praised first responders, saying in a social media post, "All of Law Enforcement and First Responders were fantastic!"

Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said that "by the grace of God, we have not lost one soul" during the collision and subsequent rescue.

Following the rescue mission, the US Coast Guard has reopened the main channel to limited traffic after it was shut down immediately following the collision, Burnham said.

It could take weeks to remove the American Heritage from the river, the mayor said. Before the riverboat is moved, Burnham said, its 16,000 gallons of fuel need to be removed.

In the initial phase of the NTSB investigation, officials recovered the tanker's voyage data recorder, according to John DeLeeuw, an NTSB board member. The device is similar to a flight data recorder on airplanes, and it tracks information including the ship's maneuvers, course and audio from the bridge, Andrew Ehlers, deputy director of marine safety at NTSB, told reporters Saturday afternoon.

Investigators will be at the collision scene for about a week, DeLeeuw said. Officials will interview crew members and others involved, and they will work to collect any remaining evidence on scene, including from the river boat that is partially submerged in about 25 feet of water.

The NTSB will issue its preliminary report in about a month, followed by a final report released between 18 and 24 months later, DeLeeuw said.

Landry said there "is an active investigation" into the collision.

"We want to make sure that this investigation is thorough, we understand exactly what happened, so that we can triage those problems and ensure that the Mississippi River remains a very safe place," he said.

This story has been updated with additional information.

CNN's Aaron Cooper, Sarah Dewberry, Taylor Galgano, Jason Morris, Jada Furlow and Shawn Nottingham contributed to this report

articles.title: A Pennsylvania father threatened not to take his daughters to school if their mother came for a first-day photo, and barred her from tennis matches; appeals judges upheld her control of activities on November 12
articles.summary: A custody dispute can become particularly difficult when parents struggle to cooperate over their children's everyday activities and important milestones.
articles.body: A custody dispute can become particularly difficult when parents struggle to cooperate over their children's everyday activities and important milestones. In Pennsylvania, a father who objected to the mother's involvement in the children's school events and extracurricular activities challenged a custody order giving her sole decision-making authority over those activities. The Pennsylvania Superior Court, in a November 12, 2026 memorandum decision available on Justia, upheld the arrangement, finding no abuse of discretion in the lower court's custody determination.The case involved John M Surma and Julie S Surma, who share two daughters. Although both parents retained shared physical and legal custody, the trial court gave the mother sole legal custody over the children's extracurricular activities. The father appealed, arguing that the court had made errors in evaluating the evidence and determining the custody arrangements.Dispute over school events and children's activitiesThe custody proceedings had been ongoing since 2019, following the father's divorce and custody filings. Both parents had previously been granted shared legal and physical custody. However, disagreements over parenting arrangements, communication and the children's activities continued, eventually leading the father to seek another modification in May 2024. During the custody proceedings, the mother testified that she regularly offered the daughters different extracurricular activities and allowed them to choose which ones they wanted to pursue. She also placed the schedules on a shared calendar and welcomed the father to attend.However, she said the father did not extend the same opportunity to her. According to her testimony, he prevented her from attending school events, award ceremonies, piano recitals and birthday parties when these took place during his custody periods. She also said he had threatened to withhold the children's scheduled video calls with her if she attended certain events.The dispute extended to sporting activities. The mother was not allowed to watch the girls' tennis matches at the father's country club. The trial court also noted that the father sometimes failed to take the children to activities arranged by their mother when they fell on his custody days. The lower court found that his behaviour reflected an unwillingness to encourage the children's continuing relationship with their mother. It considered this particularly important when assessing the level of cooperation and conflict between the parents.Court examines parents' conduct and children's interestsThe trial court also considered other incidents that highlighted the difficulties in the parents' relationship. These included disagreements over custody exchanges, repeated police involvement and disputes about the children's telephone and video calls.One incident involved the younger daughter suffering a broken arm while in the father's care. After hospital visits, the father returned the child to his home and left her with a nanny while he went back to work, rather than allowing her to spend that time with her mother. The court also examined the father's use of software to track the duration of the children's video calls with each parent. He argued that the difference in call lengths was unfair, but the trial court found that he had sometimes ended or withheld the mother's calls.Both parents had made negative comments about each other in front of the children, and the court acknowledged that the mother was not entirely without fault. Nevertheless, it found that the father's conduct contributed significantly to the conflict and could eventually affect the children's emotional well-being. The court concluded that the daughters were doing well in school and had good relationships with their friends, but their parents needed to reduce the tension surrounding their custody arrangements.Appeals court upholds mother's authority over activitiesThe father challenged several aspects of the amended custody order, arguing that the trial court had exceeded the scope of his original modification petition and had incorrectly assessed the evidence. He also objected to the mother's sole legal authority over extracurricular activities, arguing that it could allow her to exclude him from an important part of the children's lives. The Pennsylvania Superior Court rejected his arguments. It explained that once a custody modification is under consideration, the trial court can examine the relevant arrangements more broadly, provided the parties receive proper notice and an opportunity to be heard.On the extracurricular activities issue, the appeals judges found that the lower court had properly considered the children's best interests and the parents' inability to cooperate in this area. The evidence of the father's restrictions on the mother's attendance at school and sporting events supported the decision. The appeals court also upheld the other challenged arrangements, including the requirement that custody exchanges take place at school to reduce conflict between the parents. It agreed that continuing daily video calls with the non-custodial parent served the children's interests.On November 12, 2026, the Pennsylvania Superior Court affirmed the amended final custody order, leaving the shared physical custody arrangement and the mother's sole legal authority over extracurricular activities in place. The decision is a non-precedential memorandum, meaning it does not establish binding precedent for other Pennsylvania cases.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.summary: London: A British judge has ordered the extradition of wealthy British Indian businessman Sukhjit Singh Ghuman to the US to face charges of smuggling
articles.body: London: A British judge has ordered the extradition of wealthy British Indian businessman Sukhjit Singh Ghuman to the US to face charges of smuggling foreign unapproved medical drugs from India, Sri Lanka and Turkey into the US as well as fraudulently obtaining millions of dollars from US health insurance plans, including Medicare.The allegations are that Sukhjit Singh Ghuman (48) and his former wife Kiranjit Ghuman (48) obtained cheap, unapproved chemotherapy drugs from overseas and used them on cancer patients at oncology clinics they controlled in California and Arizona. They then caused the clinics to bill Medicare and other health insurance providers as though more costly drugs approved by the US FDA had been given to the cancer patient, pocketing the difference for financial gain. The couple fraudulently billed Medicare for over $9.6 million.District judge Nina Tempia did not agree that Kiranjit's involvement in the alleged fraud "was limited", pointing out that Kiranjit controlled the clinics in Arizona and California as senior vice-president of Colton Health, LLC and she "played an active role in the clinics". articles.title: Holly Humberstone on her identity crisis - and struggle being compared to other pop stars
articles.summary: The singer felt forced to compete with her female peers, until she realised the power of longevity.
articles.body:
You might know her as a pop star, endorsed by everyone from Taylor Swift to Sam Fender, but Holly Humberstone has a secret double life.

In her spare time, the singer-songwriter is literally a cat burglar.

"We've stolen one of our neighbours' cats by accident," she laughs, in a Zoom call from her fixer-upper in New Cross, south-east London.

"He's a tiny little black cat who's come into our garden and simply chosen us."

Under the slightest scrutiny, however, her story crumbles like a biscuit in a hot cup of tea.

"OK, we've been coercing him into the house with treats," she admits. "He's just so cute.

"But we're not trying to keep him. We literally push him out every night."

Humberstone's excuse for this feline felony is that, last year, her parents sold her childhood home in Lincolnshire and moved to Wales – taking her pets with them.

One, a cat called Tsuki, had even been immortalised in the song Lucy as a confidante who listens to her problems but "never judges".

"Oh, she knows some secrets!" laughs the singer. "I'm so glad she can't talk."

"We actually tried to bring her to London with us, but she's a countryside cat and she hated it so much. We had to send her to Wales where she can be free and frolic."

Her parents' relocation was disruptive for the human Humberstones, too.

Their house, a "freezing cold, falling down" property 20 minutes outside of Grantham, played a huge part in the singer's success.

Her early EPs were all written there, inspiring the "wonky sonics" of her indie-leaning pop sound. The 2021 single Haunted House is even dedicated to the "friendly" spirits who inhabited the property.

"It's a place I always felt I could go back to, to remind myself of who I am," she says.

Instead, she spent 2025 "packing up 23 years of stuff my family and I had accumulated", from her old ballet shoes and poetry books to forgotten bits of jewellery.

The process was unsettling. Already grappling with the idea of leaving childhood behind, Humberstone found herself literally throwing away her past.

"I felt uprooted. I was having some sort of identity crisis almost weekly," she says.

So she did what she's always done, and poured those feelings into her second album, Cruel World, which entered the UK charts at number four earlier this year.

"Writing these songs felt like building myself a little shield and a kind of safety bubble," she says. "There's an escapist, fantasy element to so much of the album."

Maybe that's true, but Humberstone has always had the ability to locate a song's emotional core, and the lyrics on Cruel World don't disappoint.

" To lose somebody is to know you're only human, honey, " she sings on To Love Somebody , soothing her elder sister as she endures an agonising break-up.

Undeterred by that heartbreak, she throws herself headfirst into a new affair on Die Happy , declaring: " Hit the gas, I want it fast, want it reckless ."

But the most revealing song is the closing track, Beauty Pageant .

Fragile and raw, it's the sound of Humberstone in her dressing room, addressing the woman in the mirror who'd "die for the applause" but who struggles with the impossible beauty standards imposed on female artists.

"That's a song that I wasn't really setting out to write," she confesses.

"Writing about other people often feels easier than turning the magnifying glass on yourself."

The lyrics, she says, draw on a "very specific" mindset she acquired at her all-girls school in Grantham.

"It was drilled into me: You're all in competition. You're only rewarded if you're the best. And if you're not, you're worthless."

The experience "really warped the way I view other girls", she says.

Musical success made it worse. After winning the Brits Rising Star award in 2022 , Humberstone found herself competing with megastars, even though her music leaned towards the alternative side of pop.

"I'm a very small fish and I recognise that, but suddenly I was in meetings being compared to all these people on my label's roster, who are on a completely different scale," she says.

"It's something I really, really struggled with in the early days and it's something I've really had to unlearn."

Nowadays, Humberstone has stopped benchmarking herself against her peers, recognising that the need for validation never fades.

"I don't think that there's a point I could get to, or an award that I could win, where these feelings would disappear," she says.

"Everybody feels like they've still got something to prove, so I'm done with setting myself goals - because then I lose sight of the real reason that I'm doing this, which is to write music that represents me, and have other people feel understood through that music."

That mindset comes to fruition in the new, expanded edition of Cruel World, whose five new songs were largely written after the original album was handed in.

"I was super proud of Cruel World and, when you've got that in your back pocket, there's room to experiment and break some of your usual parameters."

The new tracks find Humberstone embracing a new persona – more confident, more flirtatious, a little salty – with music inspired by a playlist featuring Abba, Madonna and Robyn.

The single Too Cute To Be Lonely is a will-they/won't-they story set at a house party.

" Don't leave a girl upset, in such a pretty dress ," she teases the object of her affections.

Terminally Yours takes place a couple of weeks later, when Humberstone realises she's fallen head-over-heels in love.

" Your stupid face is my sorry fate ," she harrumphs, cross at herself. " For [expletive]'s sake, I'm in love ."

Silver Sky, a gorgeous acoustic ballad, tells another side of the story, as she settles into her lover's arms and drifts into blissful reverie.

"I wrote that on a kind of Hail Mary trip, seeing what fell out of the air in Nashville," she reveals.

"We went over to [co-writer Maddie Diaz's] house, took a guitar into the garden and wrote Silver Sky outside, while all of these gorgeous red cardinals were singing around us.

"I usually write a lot about my mental health struggles, but I was just in the mood to write something that made me feel good."

Not that her mental health issues are in the rear view mirror. Humberstone admits her stage nerves have only intensified since the release of Cruel World.

"It's the proudest I've been of any of my work and, for that reason, I struggled with shows because I felt a lot of pressure to go out and deliver it to the standard that I think people are expecting.

"But on the other hand, it's totally fine if you mess up or sing a wrong note. People can't connect to a pop star that feels too robotic and polished.

"So maybe my strength is that vulnerability, and I need to recognise that more."

That vulnerability has won Humberstone millions of fans, even if a hit single has (so far) eluded her.

And her audience keeps growing. In May this year, her breakout single Falling Asleep At The Wheel was awarded a silver disc... five years after its release, indicating that her songs have staying power in an era of disposable hits.

Astonishingly, this is news to Humberstone, who learns about the accolade during our interview. But it helps to clarify a thought that's been knocking around her head.

"If I'm going to be doing this for years to come, I've just got to keep making music that feels right, trusting my gut and realising there's no end point," she says.

"Reaching an end point would mean I've 'made it', but I think, maybe, that's a myth that doesn't really exist."

articles.title: Australian buyer agreed to pay $2.2 million for land advertised for 15 homes and paid a $220,000 deposit; court upholds its decision to walk away after subdivision approval remains unresolved
articles.summary: An Australian property buyer has recovered a $220,000 deposit after a court upheld its decision to terminate a $2.2 million land purchase involving a
articles.body: An Australian property buyer has recovered a $220,000 deposit after a court upheld its decision to terminate a $2.2 million land purchase involving a proposed 15-home development. The dispute arose when planning approval left important details of the subdivision unresolved, despite the seller having represented that the land would be divided into 15 lots. The Queensland Court of Appeal ruled that the buyer had a valid contractual basis to walk away, finding that uncertainty surrounding the approval supported its concerns about whether the promised development could proceed as expected.Why did the Australian property buyer terminate the $2.2 million dealBrades Property Agnes Water Pty Ltd had agreed to sell land to Skyrock Sun Pty Ltd for $2.2 million, reports Case Law Wire. The buyer was to put down a $220,000 deposit in the transaction which would split the property into 15 residential lots.Prior to signing the agreement, the seller’s real estate agent had represented that the land would be subdivided into 15 lots. That statement was particularly important as the proposed development was key to the buyer’s decision to acquire the property.The sale agreement signed on July 5, 2022, included special conditions relating to the development approval. These conditions enabled the buyer to determine whether the approval was consistent with the seller’s representations, whether its requirements were normal for such developments and whether any provision reduced the proposed number of lots to less than 15.Fraser Lawyers, in its analysis of the case, explained that the wording of these conditions ultimately determined whether the buyer could terminate the transaction and recover its deposit.What made the planning approval insufficient for the buyerThe development application had sought approval to reconfigure the property into a 15-lot subdivision. However, the approval issued by Gladstone Regional Council on 25 August 2022 did not include an approved or stamped subdivision plan.The approval also required revised subdivision plans to be lodged with the council before an application for operational works was lodged, Case Law Wire reported. Another condition required more information on the capacity of a rubble pit to handle stormwater, and changes to the detention strategy may be required.These requirements introduced uncertainty about the final development layout. In an email dated September 1, 2022, the council said meeting the conditions could alter the proposed layout and impact the number and design of lots.The buyer was told this before the agreement was canceled, said Fraser Lawyers. The council's warning became a significant part of the evidence supporting the buyer's concerns.The court examined the buyer's satisfaction clauseThe Queensland Court of Appeal considered the dispute in Brades Property Agnes Water Pty Ltd v Skyrock Sun Pty Ltd [2026] QCA 141, decided on 28 July 2026.The appeal was heard by Kelly J, Mullins P and Boddice JA and the reasons agreed, according to Fraser Lawyers. The court dismissed the appeal unanimously, upholding the earlier finding that the buyer validly terminated the contract.The big question was what the satisfaction clause in the agreement meant. The court held that satisfaction of the purchaser was a condition precedent to the court's unconditional obligation to complete the purchase.However, the buyer could not simply reject the deal for any reason. Its dissatisfaction had to be honest and reasonable, considering the information available at the time.Why the unresolved subdivision matteredThe seller’s representatives contended that the development approval described a subdivision into 15 lots and that the contractual requirements were satisfied. But the court held that the practical consequences of the approval could not be divorced from the seller's earlier statement that the property would be subdivided into 15 lots.As Case Law Wire explained, the relevant question was not simply whether the approval legally authorised a 15-lot development. It was whether the buyer could reasonably remain dissatisfied when the approval left important matters unresolved.The absence of an approved subdivision plan, the requirement for revised plans and the council's warning about possible changes to the layout all supported the buyer's position.The court did not determine that the approval legally permitted fewer than 15 lots. Rather, it found that the unresolved planning requirements were relevant to whether the buyer's dissatisfaction was reasonable.The $220,000 deposit remained recoverableThe deposit was paid by the buyer on 8 July 2022 and then released to the seller pursuant to a separate agreement between the parties. Under that arrangement, the deposit was treated as a loan, and the obligation to repay was triggered by the termination or completion of the sale.It demanded repayment after the buyer terminated the agreement on 21 September 2022. The seller refused and there was a dispute as to the lawfulness of the termination. The seller’s appeal was dismissed by the Queensland Court of Appeal and ordered it to pay the buyer’s costs of appeal.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

articles.title: UK government to consider changing age of consent after allegations against Russell Brand
articles.summary: Deputy prime minister says change would be a massive step but ‘deserves proper consideration and scrutiny’
articles.body:
The government has said it will consider calls to change the age of consent after a woman waived her right to anonymity to publicly claim she was raped by Russell Brand as a 16-year-old schoolgirl.

Mia Latter, now 37, alleged she had been orally raped by the jailed comedian when she was a teenager and he was 30 years old.

In an interview with the Sunday Times, she called for the introduction of a staggered age of consent – which would make relationships between adults and teenagers aged 16 and 17 illegal.

Louise Haigh, the de facto deputy prime minister, told the newspaper that Latter's "heart-breaking story" meant a law change deserved consideration.

She said: "We need to listen to Mia and other victims like her who have been through these experiences because it's really important that as lawmakers their experience is at the heart of what we consider.

"It clearly would be a massive step to change the age of consent, but it deserves proper consideration and scrutiny. I can absolutely understand why she is calling for it."

Under UK law, adults of any age are legally able to have sex with 16 and 17-year-olds.

Latter said: "It's shocking to me time and time again that whenever the news comes up again about him, it's always in the comments about the relationship with a 16-year-old.

"That's not the most heinous bit. But why is that the thing that everybody collectively gets stuck on? I think we all sort of agree that … adults shouldn't be allowed to have sexual relationships with children, with somebody under the age of 18. That really doesn't seem like a gigantic leap to take."

Latter was referred to under the pseudonym of Alice in previous reporting by the Sunday Times, the Times, and Channel 4's Dispatches documentary.

She was 16 when she first met Brand in Leicester Square, central London, while she was on her way home from a shopping trip.

He took her number and later messaged her, asking if she wanted to go for dinner, she said.

She told the newspaper that Brand – who was working at MTV at the time – still asked her to meet after she had confessed her age to him.

Latter alleges Brand orally raped her towards the end of their three-month relationship.

Brand denied all of the allegations made against him by Latter when they were first reported in 2023 by the Times.

She spoke to the police after the documentary, but the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) decided not to include her case in Brand's trial at Southwark Crown Court.

He was convicted of attacks against four of the six women who gave evidence against him, and is now serving a 10-and-a-half-year prison term for one count of rape and three sexual assaults.

Earlier this week, it was announced that a series of "serious" sex offence allegations against comedian David Walliams are being probed by the Metropolitan police after an investigation by the Guardian and ITV News.

One woman described her alleged encounter with Walliams when she was 15 as "sexual assault".

Haigh went on to say that, in light of news that one of Walliams's accusers was asked to sign a non disclosure agreement (NDA), the government should also look at banning them in cases of alleged sexual assault and harassment. She said: "When we consider the allegations against David Walliams, teenagers who were fans wouldn't come under the current consultation.

"I do think there is a very strong case to look at banning NDAs in all circumstances where they relate to harassment or discrimination, to make sure that no victim, regardless of where it happened or what their relationship was with the perpetrator, should ever be silenced."

It is believed MPs outside Labour may support a bill to change the age of consent laws, with Jess Brown-Fuller, the Liberal Democrat justice spokesperson, coming out in favour of reviewing them.

Commending Latter for the "extraordinary bravery" it took to waive her anonymity, Brown-Fuller said: "I think we must go further to increase protections for young women and girls, and looking at a staggered age of consent is an important step.

"We already have rules that recognise power imbalances in professions: between teachers and students, or barristers and junior colleagues. It's time for the government to recognise the implicit power imbalance held by older men over teenage girls."

Latter's decision to come forward was also praised by Bridget Phillipson, the minister for women and equalities, who said she "and thousands of others across the country will be in awe of her courage and determination". She added that it is "up to all of us to send a message to women and girls who experience sexual violence: the shame is not yours. Women like Mia are leading the charge, but we can and must do more to make this a moment of change."

Latter's allegation was reported to the Met police, who said the investigation into the alleged rape remains ongoing.

A Met Police spokesperson said: "Officers launched an investigation in January 2026 after receiving an allegation of rape.

"Detectives sought advice from the Crown Prosecution Service to determine how best to proceed, and officers were advised that further information was needed before a charging decision could be made.

"This investigation remains ongoing. We understand the delay has been distressing for this victim-survivor. However, our focus has been on putting forward the best possible evidence."

The CPS said: "The Crown Prosecution Service will continue to work closely with investigators to provide advice and make sure cases progress as quickly as possible."

articles.body: Washington: The nationwide ground stop that led to thousands of flight cancellations in US was the first since Jan 2023, when another key Federal Aviation Administration computer system that sends notices to pilots malfunctioned, and the second since the Sept 11, 2001, attacks.Andrew Charlton, an aviation consultant, said the stoppage on Friday had affected about a quarter of the 45,000 flights in the US each day."The knock-on effect of that is incredible," said Charlton, managing director of Aviation Advocacy. "The aircraft doesn't just fly from A to B and back to B and then stop. It then moves onto C and then over to E and around and around and around. It is, of course, exacerbated if you're talking about long-haul flights, international flights over the Atlantic or over the Pacific."At airports across the US, passengers stared at screens showing delays or rushed to find buses or trains to their destinations. Emily Brown and her 14-year-old daughter waited more than four hours Friday at the Dallas airport for their flight to Columbus, Ohio, before giving up. They were travelling to surprise her daughter's best friend. Instead, she had to settle for phoning the friend through tears in the airport, Brown said."She saved up her money to buy her own ticket, and she's planned this whole weekend," Brown said. "Now we're not sure when we're gonna be able to go."More than 2,500 flights were cancelled in the US Saturday and hundreds more were delayed, according to FlightAware, a website that tracks flight disruptions.At London's Heathrow Airport, several flights to and from the US were listed as delayed or cancelled Saturday, including American Airlines flights to Dallas and Los Angeles, and a British Airways flight to New York's JFK Airport. A Delta flight from Atlanta, an American flight from Miami and a United flight from Chicago were also listed as cancelled.Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin told reporters at the White House that no one was in any danger as more than 3,000 flights in the air at the time of the grounding order landed safely Friday.US transportation secretary Sean Duffy blamed Congress for failing to approve more funding for new technology, while downplaying the fact that trying to implement new fixes overtaxed the system. He suggested more disruptions might occur. "We didn't think we would have this kind of outage. We did," he said. "We were able to review what went wrong, and then reboot the system and go. Fasting devotees stand in the water and offer milk and water to the setting sun. It is one of the oldest ways to say thank you, directed at the source of light and life itself.Chapter 3 Verse 11 of the Bhagavad Gita explains why such thanks matter. Krishna tells Arjuna to nourish the devas through offering, so that the devas in turn nourish people. By supporting one another in this way, he says, both reach the highest good. The very next verse adds that anyone who enjoys these gifts without offering anything back is no better than a thief.Parasparam Means MutualThe key word here is parasparam, meaning each other. Life in the Gita runs on a cycle of giving and receiving.Sunlight grows the crops. An offering of thanks completes the circle.Taking Without Thanks Breaks the CycleKrishna’s word for the one who only takes is stena, a thief. It is a blunt label, chosen on purpose.In daily life, this can look like accepting a parent’s help for years without a word of thanks. The help may continue, but something in the relationship thins.Gratitude Shifts AttentionA short thank-you each morning trains the mind to notice what is already working. Over months, this changes how problems get approached.A person who sees support around them tends to act with more confidence.Destiny Grows From Small HabitsIn the Gita’s view, actions repeated daily shape what follows. Gratitude is one such action.A habit of giving thanks builds goodwill with colleagues and neighbours alike. That goodwill often returns in ways nobody planned.Arjuna’s Strength Had Many SourcesKrishna’s teaching on offering reminded Arjuna that many hands shaped his skill and standing.Duty, in this light, became a way of giving back.Evening at the GhatVerse 11 of Chapter 3 links thankful offering with shared wellbeing. Chhath gives that idea a powerful public form.At a ghat in Patna tonight, an elderly woman stands waist-deep in the river as the sun sets. articles.title: ‘Society’s in bad shape’: More than 100,000 protest across France for fifth consecutive weekend
articles.summary: More than 100,000 people took to the streets across France on Saturday for the fifth consecutive weekend of protests, voicing concerns over the rising
articles.body: More than 100,000 people took to the streets across France on Saturday for the fifth consecutive weekend of protests, voicing concerns over the rising cost of living, education funding, children's rights and a proposed law granting greater protection to police officers using firearms.The demonstrations brought together the Yellow Vest movement, students, education unions and other activists. The French interior ministry put the nationwide turnout at around 106,000, including 24,000 in Paris.Organisers, however, estimated that 200,000 people participated, with nearly 100,000 in the capital, according to Euronews.The protests were largely peaceful, although clashes and the use of tear gas were reported in several cities.In Paris, demonstrators gathered at Place de la Republique, a regular meeting point for nationwide protests. Students demanded better funding for education, adequate facilities in schools and improved access to higher education."We’re asking to have teachers when we go to class. We’re asking to not have ceilings collapsing on us when we eat in the canteen. We’re asking, when we get our A-levels, despite conditions getting worse every year, to be able to carry on our studies at university," Marius Mesnil, co-secretary-general of the Union Syndicale Lycéenne, said.The protests have been accompanied by school blockades, strikes and demonstrations for more than a month. Participants have raised concerns over falling educational standards, low wages, rising living costs and alleged police violence. Some also carried placards targeting President Emmanuel Macron.Turnout lower than previous protestsSaturday's demonstrations drew fewer people than the previous weekend, when authorities estimated that 146,000 people had participated nationwide, including 46,000 in Paris.The largest mobilisation in recent weeks took place during a union-led strike on Thursday last week, when more than half a million people took to the streets across France, according to official figures.Protests in Marseille continued despite a weekend ban imposed by the local authorities. The prefecture estimated that around 3,500 people took part in the demonstrations there. Local media reported the use of tear gas and a water cannon, as well as fires in a public square.In Lyon, around 8,000 people reportedly participated, with local media showing masked demonstrators chanting near street fires as police used tear gas. Tear gas was also reported in Nantes, Bordeaux and Paris.The demonstrations have faced increased police deployment and tighter controls on transport and protest permits following incidents of violence and looting during some earlier rallies.Protesters oppose proposed police firearms lawA major focus of Saturday's demonstrations was opposition to a proposed police bill that would give police officers and gendarmes greater protection when using firearms in the line of duty.Supporters, including Marine Le Pen's far-right National Rally party, argue that the legislation is needed to prevent officers from being automatically presumed guilty of using excessive force.Unions and civil rights activists, however, say the proposed measure would make it harder to hold law enforcement officials accountable. They have described it as a "licence to kill"."What the so-called 'licence to kill' law, which is being put to the vote next week, provides for is literally that a police officer who fires will first be presumed to have acted lawfully," Sabrine Kharbach, spokesperson for the Student Union, said."Yet another layer of impunity for those who club us, gas us and maim us. Yet another layer of impunity for this police force that acts as the armed wing of the state," she added.The bill has been approved by the lower house and is due to go before the Senate, AFP reported.The issue has also drawn criticism from lawyers representing people injured during recent demonstrations. Last week, lawyers representing at least 18 protesters said they would sue the interior ministry over its alleged responsibility for police brutality.They accused officers of using excessive force that resulted in serious injuries, including to protesters' hands, feet and eyes.Unions call fresh strike for TuesdayUnions have announced another day of strike action for Tuesday after rejecting the government's promise to increase the minimum wage by 0.6%, describing the proposed rise as inadequate."The government has only given us crumbs, and we want the whole bakery," Benjamin Ball, a member of the Yellow Vest movement, said.The next round of protests would coincide with the eighth anniversary of the Yellow Vest movement, which began in 2018 with demonstrations against rising fuel prices and went on to trigger two years of protests during the early part of Macron's presidency.Activists have also been demanding stronger safeguards for children and teenagers, including better protection against sexual abuse. Claire Bourdille, from a collective campaigning against violence against children, said the different demands reflected wider social concerns."Society's in bad shape," she said. "We can't focus on one cause more than another."The protests come ahead of France's presidential election next year, with the far right viewing the contest as an opportunity to gain power.You use AI every day. articles.title: Quote of the day by Pablo Picasso: "We artists are indestructible; even in a prison, or in a concentration camp, I would be...paint my pictures with my wet tongue on the dusty floor of my cell"
articles.summary: Pablo Picasso was a Spanish painter, sculptor, and printmaker who is popularly known as one of the most influential artists of the 20th century.
articles.body: Pablo Picasso was a Spanish painter, sculptor, and printmaker who is popularly known as one of the most influential artists of the 20th century.He co-founded the Cubist movement and also helped invent collage and constructed sculpture. But beyond art, he was also known for his sharp, witty remarks about art, which continue to be relevant even today.He once spoke about the profound idea of the power that lives inside artists, no matter where they get it, and that they are capable of creating something powerful and profound enough to evoke emotions.Let us read further to know what he meant exactly.Quote of the dayWe artists are indestructible; even in a prison, or in a concentration camp, I would be almighty in my own world of art, even if I had to paint my pictures with my wet tongue on the dusty floor of my cellWhat does the quote mean?The quote says that an artist's power lives inside them, not in their tools or surroundings. Even if one takes away the studio, the paints, even personal freedom, the artist still has imagination.The words creating ‘the image of painting with a wet tongue on a dusty cell floor’ describe making something out of almost nothing, explaining the power of art. The phrase "almighty in my own world of art" is about inner freedom. It doesn't mean that being in a prison is acceptable. It says that walls cannot reach the part of a person who creates.Sites like Goodreads and AZQuotes attribute the quote to Pablo Picasso, printing it under his name. According to Wikiquote, a 1951 account says Picasso told a woman he could paint anywhere, and that even in prison he would draw on the dusty walls and floor with his finger wet with spit, so even though these words have been attributed to Picasso, the spirit of his ideas has hardly aged.How is the idea still relevant?Many people feel their creativity depends on the right equipment, budget, or audience. Jobs disappear, and platforms and algorithms change overnight. In many countries, writers, painters, and musicians still face censorship or pressure. The quote reminds us that the urge to create is hard to switch off, and all that you need to start is what you have, whether that's a pencil, a phone, or a notebook.You use AI every day. articles.title: Psychology says women who don’t wear makeup tend to care less about external validation and have a deep underlying confidence
articles.summary: Makeup can alter a woman’s appearance, but does the feeling of beauty truly depend on using it?
articles.body: Makeup can alter a woman’s appearance, but does the feeling of beauty truly depend on using it? Many women like applying cosmetics to accentuate their features, whereas others prefer going out without makeup and feel equally at ease. Though it may seem like a mere question of taste, psychology provides a deeper understanding of the connection between makeup, self-esteem, and the desire for external validation.The study, titled 'The contrasting effects of body image and self-esteem in the makeup usage', indicates that makeup can help women feel more attractive and more satisfied with the way they look. At the same time, some research has found that women reach for cosmetics more often when they feel less physically attractive. That leads to a fair question: are women who feel comfortable without makeup less dependent on external validation?When makeup lifts confidence, and its absence brings discomfortThe study done on 50 Brazilian women titled 'Makeup and its application simulation affect women's self-perceptions' was published in the archives of sexual behaviour journal, in November 2021. It was an experimental study where they saw themselves with and without makeup; participants described themselves as more feminine and more attractive after the makeup had been applied by a professional. They also reported being happier with their appearance and having higher self-esteem.Another study, called 'Effects of cosmetics use on the physical attractiveness and body image of american college women', published in 1989 in the Journal of Social Psychology, pointed the same way. Women gave themselves higher attractiveness ratings when wearing their usual facial cosmetics than when they were taken off. Together, these findings suggest that makeup can shape how women view themselves. It can raise their perceived attractiveness and offer a temporary confidence boost.However, a flip side of it also talks about how women who rated their own physical attractiveness lower tended to use more makeup. This hints that cosmetics can sometimes become a tool for improving how women feel about their looks or for managing how they expect others to see them. For some women, makeup is a joyful form of self-expression. For others, it can turn into something they feel they must have before facing the world. What separates the two is whether cosmetics are a personal choice or a source of reassurance about their appearance.Does wearing less makeup mean caring less about what others think?The link between makeup and self-esteem is far from straightforward. Research has produced conflicting results on whether women who use more cosmetics have higher or lower self-esteem. One study of 30 British undergraduate women found a negative relationship between self-esteem and cosmetic use, meaning women with lower self-esteem tended to wear more makeup. But some people had a positive association between self-esteem and makeup use. Such differences may stem from the cultural and demographic backgrounds of the participants. They also show why makeup habits alone cannot tell us how confident a woman is. The findings raise an intriguing possibility: women who are comfortable appearing without makeup may depend less on cosmetics to feel attractive or socially accepted. Instead of worrying about whether their looks meet other people's expectations, they may feel the the freedom to present themselves naturally as they are.Wanting to look beautiful versus feeling you have toThere is an important psychological gap between enjoying makeup and feeling unable to go without it. A woman who wears lipstick because she loves the shade or who experiments with eye makeup because she enjoys the process is expressing a personal preference. But someone who feels anxious about being seen without foundation or who worries that others will judge their natural face may be dealing with appearance-related pressure. The researchers also found that the questionnaire could predict self-objectification, as well as concerns about body shape and weight.Self-objectification happens when women start judging their appearance from an outsider's point of view, concentrating on how others might see and assess their bodies. This suggests that the pressure to look a certain way reaches beyond beauty routines. It can also influence how women perceive themselves. For women who are comfortable going without makeup, not feeling forced to meet these expectations may be an important part of their relationship with confidence.You use AI every day.
