articles.title: Cede Donbas to Russia to join Nato, US tells Ukraine
articles.summary: Kyiv: US negotiators have floated the idea of Ukraine's potential withdrawal from its eastern region of Donbas in exchange for joining Nato, President
articles.body: Kyiv: US negotiators have floated the idea of Ukraine's potential withdrawal from its eastern region of Donbas in exchange for joining Nato, President Volodymyr Zelensky said, following the latest round of peace talks with Russia in Abu Dhabi.This is the first time the question of linking Nato membership to territorial concessions has been raised during the talks, Zelensky said in remarks to reporters released by his office on Saturday. "The Americans raised a question: 'What if Ukraine joins Nato? Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?'" he said."That is why I believe Nato is back on the agenda. But you have also heard (Russian President Vladimir) Putin's signals, and this is an extremely difficult conversation." Putin has long said Ukrainian membership of Nato is a red line for Moscow, citing the issue as one reason for launching Russia's full-blown invasion in 2022.Zelensky reiterated that Kyiv was not ready to concede territory but said that if it received a comprehensive package including security guarantees, the right to a strong and well-funded Ukrainian army and funds to rebuild, he would put the question to a national referendum.Zelensky rejects security talks before peace dealEchoing comments made by European leaders at a summit in Dublin Friday, Zelensky dismissed Russia's call for a broad agreement on European security architecture to be reached before the specifics of how to end the war in Ukraine are agreed on. "We cannot turn everything upside down and start by talking about changing the security framework in the world or across the continent overall, and only then talk about ending this war. This war must be ended first," he said.Zelensky also dismissed Putin's suggestion for a local humanitarian ceasefire in Kostiantynivka, a hotly contested city in Ukraine's eastern Donetsk region, saying it reflected Moscow's inability to take the city by force.Civilians there have already had the opportunity to evacuate, he added. "Putin simply wants us to leave Kostiantynivka so that they can move in and occupy the entire city that way," he said.Ukraine has given a list of seven or eight other frontline settlements where civilians, including children, are trapped for a potential humanitarian truce, but Russia prefers to use them as military targets, Zelensky said.Moscow denies deliberately targeting civilians in the war. The two days of US-brokered talks between Ukraine and Russia concluded on Wednesday in the Emirati capital without a major breakthrough, though the sides agreed to a prisoner exchange that will involve more than 1,000 people.US peace envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner had pledged to raise an energy ceasefire with Putin at a meeting in Moscow on Thursday, Zelensky said.Zelensky met Witkoff and Kushner on Thursday in Ireland after their talks in Moscow, and said the US negotiators had agreed that Europe would have a seat at the table in forthcoming peace talks.In Abu Dhabi, delegates from Europe - currently Ukraine's largest financial and military backer - had talks with US and Ukrainian officials but did not sit at the table with Russia.You use AI every day. articles.title: Prince William, Kate Middleton to attend Earthshot Prize in Mumbai in first joint overseas tour since 2022
articles.summary: Britain's Princess of Wales, Kate Middleton, will join her husband Prince William in India this week for the 2026 Earthshot Prize awards, marking her
articles.body: Britain's Princess of Wales, Kate Middleton, will join her husband Prince William in India this week for the 2026 Earthshot Prize awards, marking her biggest overseas engagement since undergoing preventative chemotherapy for cancer in 2024.The Prince and Princess of Wales, both 44, will travel to Mumbai for a three-day visit featuring events around the annual environmental awards, with the ceremony scheduled for Tuesday, November 17, according to Reuters .The visit will be their first joint overseas tour since Kate's cancer diagnosis in 2024. Their last official overseas tour together was to Boston in the United States in 2022, also for the Earthshot Prize.Kate has gradually increased her public engagements since announcing that she was in remission in early 2025. However, she has not accompanied William on his previous overseas trips for the awards, which were held in Singapore in 2023, Cape Town in 2024 and Rio de Janeiro in 2025.Her only significant overseas visit since her diagnosis before the India trip was a two-day solo engagement in Italy in May, focused on early childhood development.Earthshot Prize to host its biggest ceremony in MumbaiFounded by Prince William in 2020, the Earthshot Prize aims to identify and support solutions to climate change and other environmental challenges. Five winners receive £1 million ($1.3 million) each to help scale up their projects.The Mumbai ceremony is expected to be the biggest edition of the awards so far, bringing together around 5,000 people, including heads of state, young people, academics, scientists, businesses, innovators, philanthropists and representatives of indigenous communities, People.com reported.This year's awards received around 7,000 nominations from 169 countries, with 15 finalists selected. They include Argentina-based wildfire detection platform Satellites on Fire, the Yellowstone to Yukon conservation initiative and Mahindra Last Mile Mobility, one of India's major electric three-wheeler manufacturers.William's office at Kensington Palace said the visit would also focus on innovation, sustainability, youth leadership and the longstanding relationship between the UK and India."For the prince, Earthshot is ultimately about replacing pessimism with possibility," a spokesperson for the couple's office said."It is about demonstrating that while the environmental challenges facing our planet are serious, the ingenuity, determination and creativity being applied to solving them are every bit as powerful."The royal couple are also expected to attend events connected with Indian cricket, fashion and cinema during their stay.Sachin Tendulkar, Alia Bhatt among guestsThe awards ceremony will feature several prominent Indian and international personalities, including cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar, actor Alia Bhatt and actor Rami Malek.British pop group Take That will also perform in India for the first time at the event."To be performing here for the very first time, after all these years, and alongside the extraordinary people creating a better future for our planet - is really special," the group said in a statement.India was selected to host the 2026 awards partly because of its role in technology, biodiversity and climate initiatives. Announcing the host city in February, William highlighted India's large young population and its contribution to the Earthshot Prize.The couple also have a previous association with the country. They visited India and Bhutan in 2016, travelling to Mumbai, New Delhi, Kaziranga National Park in Assam and the Taj Mahal in Agra.Kate says cancer recovery has not been linearKate stepped back from public duties after announcing her cancer diagnosis in January 2024 and undergoing preventative chemotherapy. She revealed in early 2025 that she was in remission, while acknowledging that recovery continued to affect her life.In an interview published this week in Country Life magazine, for which William served as guest editor, she spoke about the challenges of recovery."I was told in hospital that my recovery would not be linear. There will be good days and bad days, that it will take time," she said.Since returning to public life, Kate has gradually taken on more engagements, including hosting state visits. Her May visit to Italy was her first overseas trip in more than two years.The India visit will be her first joint foreign engagement with William since his cancer diagnosis was made public, as the couple continue their overseas work alongside the environmental and other causes they support.You use AI every day. articles.title: US flight disruption to persist 'well into Sunday' as officials blame faulty router, ageing systems
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Air travel across the United States is expected to take until late Sunday to return to normal after a nationwide flight disruption caused by
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Air travel across the United States is expected to take until late Sunday to return to normal after a nationwide flight disruption caused by communication failures at air traffic control centres. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has traced the problem to maintenance work involving a telecommunications network and a potentially faulty router installed by its contractor, L3Harris, officials said on Saturday.The disruption continued to affect thousands of passengers even after the FAA lifted its nationwide ground stop on Friday evening. As of 6:45 pm ET (23:45 GMT) on Saturday, airlines had cancelled more than 6,150 flights and delayed over 7,300, according to flight-tracking website FlightAware. More than 530 flights scheduled for Sunday had also been cancelled.The disruption followed an even worse day on Friday, when airlines cancelled around 9,200 flights and delayed 7,500 after the FAA ordered a nationwide ground stop that halted nearly all departing flights for almost five hours.Also read | US transport secy blames expired tech for flight chaosFAA chief Bryan Bedford said he expected airline operations to largely return to normal by late Sunday. He apologised to passengers and said the system remained stable.The Friday shutdown was the longest nationwide halt to US air travel since the September 11, 2001, attacks and one of the worst single-day disruptions for the country's aviation sector.Maintenance work and router failure under investigationTransportation secretary Sean Duffy said the disruption may have been triggered by routine maintenance work carried out by FAA contractor L3Harris at a remote facility. The work involved switching telecommunications lines from older copper wiring to fibre-optic infrastructure.Duffy said officials were investigating whether the disruption resulted from an error by the contractor or a faulty router installed during the process."We're working to determine whether we had incompetence, meaning was it user error or installer error from L3Harris, or did they install a faulty router? We haven't determined what the fault was," Duffy told reporters at a news conference.He also questioned the contractor's role in maintaining the network.“Which begs the question for us: What did L3Harris do? Did they make mistakes yesterday?” Duffy told reporters. “They own this network. They’re our prime contractor. I can’t go somewhere else. They own it. Or was it a faulty router? And we’re going to find that out. And frankly, we’re going to hold people accountable.”Duffy described the maintenance work as a routine procedure that had been carried out across the country for decades. He said around 30% of the older copper wiring in the system was yet to be replaced, with officials working to identify the remaining locations.L3Harris said it was cooperating with the FAA's investigation.“L3Harris has been modernizing the communications infrastructure supporting the National Airspace System in close coordination with the FAA,” the contractor said in a statement. “We are supporting the FAA in its investigation to understand the conditions that led to the Nov. 13 ground stop of our nation’s air travel. L3Harris takes the nationwide ground stop and its impact on travelers, airlines and air traffic operations seriously.”Communication failures affected 17 of 22 air traffic control centresDuffy said the trouble began on Friday afternoon when air traffic control centres experienced instability in radar and communication systems. The router issue allegedly caused data overload at other communication centres, affecting their ability to exchange information."We had over 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds, and what that did was (it) gave us issues with our communication with airplanes, and it also caused some disruption with ‌our radar," Duffy added.The disruption affected 17 of the FAA's 22 en route air traffic control centres, which manage aircraft during the cruising portion of their flights.Bedford said the FAA ordered the nationwide ground stop after receiving reports of communication frequencies going in and out at multiple facilities. Controllers had to switch between primary and backup systems, while officials struggled to establish the extent of the problem.He said the decision was taken as a precaution because of the number of facilities reporting disruptions.“If that had been a single facility, we would have just worked through it,” Bedford said.He added: “But when we saw it go to two, three, 10, 17 facilities, that’s when we started to realize there was something much larger going on here.”Bedford clarified that none of the affected facilities completely lost communication systems."No facilities went dark. Nothing was fully lost," Bedford added.The FAA said it was conducting additional tests with L3Harris to determine whether any further risks remained.Officials rule out cyberattack as causeThe disruption prompted the White House to convene an emergency meeting in the Situation Room on Friday as federal agencies examined whether the failure could have been caused by a cyberattack or deliberate interference.However, Duffy and Bedford said there was no evidence to suggest that the incident was linked to a cyberattack or any other malicious activity.“A lot of questions came in yesterday. ‘Was this a, a cyber attack? Did some foreign nation attack this network?’ And the answer to that is we don’t believe so,” Duffy said.Bedford later added: “We see zero evidence of anything nefarious, and zero evidence of anything AI-related.”Airlines cancel thousands of flights as disruption continuesAlthough the FAA lifted the ground stop on Friday evening, the disruption continued as airlines struggled to reposition aircraft, flight crews and other personnel to resume regular operations.Delta Air Lines, United Airlines and American Airlines each cancelled around 25% of their flights on Saturday, while JetBlue cancelled nearly 45%, according to the report. Airlines also issued travel waivers allowing passengers to rebook flights for later dates without additional charges.The disruption left thousands of passengers stranded at airports and affected travel plans across the country. Some college football teams were also stranded on Friday, ahead of matches scheduled for Saturday.Bedford said he believed the worst of the disruption was over, but warned that the country's ageing aviation infrastructure remained vulnerable to further failures.“I do think the worst is behind us,” Bedford said, adding that the FAA expected a full recovery by Sunday ahead of a busy travel period leading up to the Thanksgiving holiday.He cautioned that the ageing technology would remain a concern until it was replaced, saying the FAA would continue investing in keeping the system operational.Duffy seeks $50 billion to upgrade air traffic control systemThe disruption has renewed concerns over the condition of the US air traffic control network, which has been affected by ageing equipment, communication failures and a shortage of several thousand air traffic controllers.Duffy called for $50 billion in additional funding to modernise the system, raising his earlier request of $30 billion. Congress had approved $12.5 billion for upgrades last year.“I think this is a sign for them to lean in,” Duffy said. “Let’s make the investments and look forward to a brighter future in aviation, a safer future, a more efficient future in aviation.”House Speaker Mike Johnson said on Saturday that he supported additional funding for the FAA and that Republicans would use their remaining time in the congressional majority to push for the investment.“We don’t really need any investigation to understand we need further investment,” Johnson said, “We’re going to work to get it done.”Republicans control Congress until next year, when Democrats are set to take over following their gains in the November 3 midterm elections.US Representatives Rick Larsen and Andre Carson, Democrats expected to lead the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee and its aviation subcommittee next year, said their panels would examine the disruption.In a joint statement on Saturday, they said their panels would "hold the administration accountable for what happened to make sure this chaos does not happen again."Larsen and Carson also said the Transportation Department had awarded contracts worth $4.3 billion since receiving the $12.5 billion allocation last year, but had spent only $1 billion so far.You use AI every day.
